title: Circus and minstrel shows crossing paths; Ma Rainey
summary: Joe still hoped for the Al G. Barnes Circus; the show dated minstrel shows and he recalls Ma Rainey in a medicine show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah. [LAUGHS] And I got such a big kick out of that, you know, especially going into these little old small towns and being noticed -- you know. That was a kind of thrill. But in the back of my mind all the time, as soon as I get a chance, I'm going with the Al G. Barnes Circus. A lot of times we'd date a circus. What I mean, we'd play, and a circus would come to the same town where we was playing, and we'd always get together, or we'd date a minstrel show come to one of these little old small towns, like Ma Rainey was on. This was after Ma Rainey had left the medicine show, and Ma Rainey was with a show called
Florida Blossom Minstrels, or Sugar Foot Green From New Orleans with Minstrels...
What medicine show was she with?

I don't know. I think it was... They had another show called Eddie Lee's Elixir that she was in, I think. I don't know; it was something. But I happen to remember seeing her one time when they came to Baton Rouge on a medicine show. A lot of medicine shows came to Baton Rouge...
How many different medicine shows would you say there were at this time?
Oh, man, they must have had dozens of them. Some of them just maybe had a banjo player.
How famous was Doc Moon's Medicine Show?
Doc Moon was one of the best. But we never really... We never played any big cities directly. We played always on the outskirts. Like, we played on the outskirts of St. Louis.
